title: Hotspot is unavailable when a secondary Wi-Fi device can be used as an AP
line: With two Wi-Fi adapters both connected, the Hotspot button now works and uses the adapter that isn't carrying your internet connection.
explanation: Handler::checkHotspotSupported() only allowed a hotspot when some Wi-Fi device was fully disconnected or the primary connection wasn't Wi-Fi, so with two connected adapters and Wi-Fi as the primary connection the button was always disabled. createHotspotInternal() also picked a device with its own loop that could land on the adapter carrying the primary connection. MR !648 adds one shared device selection used by both: prefer unused AP-capable devices, and allow reusing an active device as long as it doesn't carry the primary connection; hotspot support is also re-checked when active connections, devices or the primary connection change.

commits.message:
Allow hotspot creation on a secondary wireless device

plasma-nm currently reports hotspot creation as unsupported when every
wireless device is active and Wi-Fi is the primary connection.

This is incorrect on systems with multiple wireless devices, where a
secondary wireless device can be reused for the hotspot without
disconnecting the connection providing the machine's default connectivity.

Introduce shared hotspot device selection which ranks wireless devices
by availability and capability. Prefer unused devices, prefer AP-capable
devices over ad-hoc-only devices, and allow an active device to be reused
when it does not carry the primary connection.

Use the same selection logic for hotspot support detection and hotspot
creation so that the selected device and wireless mode cannot disagree.

Update hotspot support when wireless devices or active connections change
so the UI reflects newly available hotspot devices.

Add regression tests for hotspot device selection and AP/ad-hoc mode
selection.

BUG: 525310

media.caption: Master: two Wi-Fi adapters connected (HomeNet primary, OfficeNet secondary), Hotspot disabled with 'all wireless radios are in use'.
With MR !648, same setup: Hotspot enabled; clicking it asks NetworkManager for an AP on the OfficeNet adapter (wlan1), leaving HomeNet alone.
Still disabled when the only other adapter is unavailable and the remaining one carries the primary connection.
